I have farmed in Quzhou County for over thirty years. I never went to school, but I know this land with my hands. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize in rotation — that is what the North China Plain is good for. I have five mu of land, and I will keep them in the same double-cropping system my family has always used. I will sow improved wheat varieties in autumn after rotary tilling the field, give them winter irrigation and three more waterings in spring, and harvest in early June. Right after the wheat comes off, I will plant hybrid maize seed without plowing again — there is no time to waste between crops, and the neighbors have shown me no-tillage works fine if the wheat stubble is managed well. I buy compound fertilizer from the local shop because they stock the blends that suit our soil, and I spray pesticides when I see weeds or insects, usually a few times each season. This way gives us steady grain and reliable income, and I do not need to gamble on crops I do not understand.
